newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran building fertiliser plant with Indian firms.
newsitem.headline: Iran building fertiliser plant with Indian firms.

text.p: Iran has finalised a joint venture deal with two Indian companies to build a $350 million fertiliser plant at its Qeshm island free zone, the zone's managing director Behrouz Boushehri said on Tuesday.
He was quoted by the official IRNA news agency as saying the plant will produce 1,350 tonnes of ammonia and 2,200 tonnes of urea per day. He gave no further details.

The London-based Middle East Economic Digest (MEED) said in November the Indian Farmers Fertiliser Co-operative (IFEC) and Krishak Bharati Co-operative were taking a 60 percent stake in the project and the free zone authority the rest.
